A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same risk-sensitive diffusion research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and content can be matched despite the title change and extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian- and Cauchy-corruption experiments, diffusion-process simulations, and generative evaluations on five datasets in Sections 4–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Appendix C, including the synthetic experiments, five-dataset Table 1, and Telemonitoring PRD curves.

M1.justification: The risk-sensitive VE/VP constructions, score-training loss, and training and sampling algorithms remain substantively the same. The general-noise formula correction agrees with an existing v1 appendix derivation; additional Cauchy training guidance does not establish a redesigned procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Gaussian- and Cauchy-corrupted synthetic mixtures, MIMIC-III and WARDS time series, and Abalone, Telemonitoring, and Mushroom tabular data. v2's additional sensor, scientific, and image examples motivate applicability but are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain standard VE/VP SDE and the Risk Regressor, Risk Variable, and Risk Conditional variants. Newly discussed methods such as Ambient Diffusion and Unbiased Diffusion are related work, not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Table 1 and the evaluation prose change the declared metric from FID scores in v1 to Wasserstein distances in v2. The precise Wasserstein variant and any recomputation are unspecified. Existing preprocessing, masking, and synthetic-experiment settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The stability-interval demonstration, Gaussian and Cauchy corruption comparisons, and Telemonitoring PRD analysis are retained. Their relocation to Appendix C does not introduce new ablations, robustness tests, or supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, result error bars, or significance tests. The retained Gaussian-process uncertainty bands describe input risk, not newly introduced uncertainty estimation for experimental performance.

E6.justification: All 50 numerical entries in Table 1 are identical, including 1.865 for risk-sensitive VE SDE and 5.926 for its Risk Conditional comparator on MIMIC-III. The experimental plots and reported rankings are also retained. The metric relabeling does not demonstrate a numerical performance gain or loss.

T1.justification: v2 Definition 5 incorporates a supremum over clean-data distributions into the instability measure. Equation (54) changes the general-noise solution from minus Psi to plus Psi, agreeing with v1 Equation (75), and Corollary 5 changes the stated Cauchy weight to a squared magnitude. Most prominently presented proofs already existed in v1's appendices.

C1.justification: The central claims about risk-sensitive diffusion, Gaussian-only exact stability, and general-noise minimization remain. Claimed applicability broadens: v1 describes the problem as largely inconsequential for high-quality image synthesis, whereas v2 Section 1.2 explicitly motivates resized images and additional sensor/scientific domains.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands applicability reasoning in Section 1.2, discussing naturally available risks, proxies when risks are unavailable, and assuming Gaussian noise when its type is unknown. It also adds a Brownian-motion explanation for Gaussian-only stability. These are substantive interpretations and proposed applications, rather than new experimental validation.

D1.justification: v2 Section 6.3 explicitly specifies full-interval time sampling when applying Algorithm 1 under Cauchy perturbation. Conversely, v1's promise to release code upon acceptance disappears. These are documentation changes; the PDFs do not establish changed implementations or actual code availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds a dedicated related-work section positioning the framework against MissDiff, Ambient Diffusion, unbiased diffusion, and label-noise research. Numerous additional references support its expanded application discussion. This substantially develops research positioning beyond v1's conditional-generation comparison.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are rewritten, with new Main Theory, Wide Applications, and Related Work sections. Existing appendix derivations become an organized sequence of main-text lemmas, propositions, and proofs, while empirical material moves to Appendix C.

P2.justification: The two-column conference layout becomes a single-column manuscript with separate title and contents pages. Colored example boxes become conventional corollaries, and figures, algorithms, and Table 1 are extensively repositioned and resized. Experimental graphics are retained; the illustrative time-series plot receives larger axis labeling.

improvement.justification: The clearer theorem organization, explicit positioning against imperfect-data research, and correction of the general-noise sign modestly improve clarity and internal consistency. These benefits are tempered by unchanged experimental support, the unexplained FID-to-Wasserstein relabeling, and removal of the code-release statement.
